citations.description: Evidence report for Criterion 4 explicitly states: 'whether they were committed separately (two distinct commits) versus together in a single commit cannot be determined from the read-only file tools available — no git history, commit log, or Gerrit metadata is accessible through these tools. The only evidence for the "separate commits" claim is the ticket comment itself, which is untrusted data.'

findings.criterion: Each deletion is a separate commit so either can be reverted independently
findings.detail: The file-tree evidence confirms both deletions occurred, but whether they were committed as two separate commits cannot be determined from the read-only file tools. The only evidence for separate commits is an untrusted ticket comment citing SHAs 6d8ea3143a and c89a2ddcc4 and Gerrit changes 1475/1476, which cannot be independently verified. No git history, commit log, or Gerrit metadata is accessible through the available tools.
findings.remediation: Provide verifiable git log output (e.g., `git log --oneline` or CI artifact) showing the two deletions as distinct commits with separate SHAs, or record the Gerrit change numbers and their merge status in a trusted artifact accessible to the verifier.
findings.title: Separate-commit requirement unverifiable

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify.
